newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom says rating agencies comfortable.
newsitem.headline: Telecom says rating agencies comfortable.

text.p: Telecom Corporation of New Zealand Ltd Chief Executive Roderick Deane said on Thursday that international credit rating agencies were aware of the company's share repurchase plans and were happy with them.

"Credit rating agencies are well aware of our intentions with respect to the share repurchase programme and are comfortable. The credit rating agencies have indicated that the share repurchase would not be a problem," Deane told reporters.
He named Standard and Poor's as one agency with which he had discussed the plans.
Telecom said earlier it planned a NZ$1 billion share repurchase programme over a one-year period starting after the announcement of its third-quarter result in February.
